messages:
jess (DevEx): Heads up — hitting a weird retry/duplicate-request issue on Android when using our Kotlin SDK (Retrofit + OkHttp). Repro in sampleapp when toggling airplane mode quickly.

jess (DevEx): Repro steps: 1) start streaming REST/chunked inference call, 2) flip airplane mode on -> off within ~2s, 3) SDK retry logic kicks in and server logs show duplicate session-start tokens and we get partial responses twice.

jess (DevEx): minimal client config:
```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(true)
  .callTimeout(0, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)
  .build()
```

jess (DevEx): logs:
```
[12:03:01.123] REQUEST id=abc123 POST /v1/generate chunked
[12:03:03.456] NETWORK error: java.io.IOException: stream closed
[12:03:03.789] RETRY attempt=1 for id=abc123
[12:03:04.012] REQUEST id=abc123 POST /v1/generate chunked
[12:03:04.200] SERVER received start_token=tok-01 twice
```

sam (Android): ack, is this the streaming chunked / OkHttp body path (not gRPC)?

jess (DevEx): yes REST chunked. We're using a RetryInterceptor that tries to re-run the request on IOExceptions. Interceptor snippet below.

jess (DevEx):
```kotlin
class RetryInterceptor : Interceptor {
  override fun intercept(chain: Interceptor.Chain): Response {
    val request = chain.request()
    try {
      return chain.proceed(request)
    } catch (ioe: IOException) {
      // naive retry: re-execute the request synchronously
      return chain.call().client().newCall(request).execute()
    }
  }
}
```

lisa (QA): oof. that newCall().execute() inside an interceptor seems suspect. If the body is unrepeatable it will still be attempted.

sam (Android): yeah — interceptor re-play + streaming body = double-send. OkHttp's built-in retryOnConnectionFailure uses transparent reconnects on transport failures but it only retransmits when it can (e.g., buffered body). On Android 13+ socket semantics changed a bit, so a close can surface as an IOException and our interceptor re-sends regardless.

mike (Platform): quick idea: treat streaming generation as non-idempotent and disable automatic retries for those endpoints. We can also implement a safe rebuffering wrapper for small bodies but not for streaming.

jess (DevEx): makes sense. Two immediate actions I can take: 1) in SDK default set retryOnConnectionFailure(false) for streaming client paths, 2) change RetryInterceptor to check if request.body?.isOneShot == true -> don't retry.

sam (Android): suggested patch:
```kotlin
if (request.body?.isOneShot() == true) {
  // return original exception, bubble up to caller to decide
  throw ioe
}
```
(note: isOneShot is pseudo-code — may need to detect streaming via sink type or headers)

jess (DevEx): i'll open a quick PR with the guard and a test harness in sampleapp that toggles airplane mode. Also adding a note in the docs: "streaming endpoints are not retried automatically on transport errors".

lisa (QA): please add a regression test that asserts server received exactly one start_token when network flaps. I can add a CI job that simulates flaky net using tcpkill.

ci-bot: Created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/1789 - "RetryInterceptor resends streaming body on transport error -> duplicate start tokens"

mike (Platform): nice. longterm we should also consider a client-side idempotency token or server dedupe on start_token to be robust.

jess (DevEx): agreed. filing a follow-up to design idempotency header behavior. thx all :thumbsup:
